### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/service-sms`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via phone_number (literal, a string literal in resolveSmsTestRecipient))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SYSTEM_CTX (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via registerAction (symbol, a method of interface MailSettingsSurface))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via phone_number (literal, a string literal in resolveSmsTestRecipient))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SYSTEM_CTX (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 41 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `96564d50ebfe78985c2b7f15210067b91d3b7709` — the merge of head `f0128702e5b595c69da6aa2a58a954b0b98db9ca` into base `7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 96564d50ebfe78985c2b7f15210067b91d3b7709 && git checkout 96564d50ebfe78985c2b7f15210067b91d3b7709
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0 f0128702e5b595c69da6aa2a58a954b0b98db9ca && git checkout -B drift-repro 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0 && git merge --no-ff f0128702e5b595c69da6aa2a58a954b0b98db9ca

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7c2eab929c6b724672849c5b295fa5e2f35d04c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 · 2026-10-20T10:31Z

`os-justin` · `session_011TdZ8GjixNZFLz1xJD9zzK` (seat post #6021). Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main` `41646a5788`, not against the report (os-dev-report on #24767). Head under review:

```text
f0128702e5b595c69da6aa2a58a954b0b98db9ca
```

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Part of #24767` (half A only), line-start `Clause-②: no` in the body and the changeset. The body carries no closing keyword and names objectstack-ai/objectui#13145 as related. 8 files, +641/−20, none on a governed surface (`governedPathsIn` answers `[]`). The trial merge onto `origin/main` is clean.
2. **Half A, read in the code.**
   - `resolveMailTestRecipient` (plugin-email) and `resolveSmsTestRecipient` (service-sms) take the request's `to` first, unchanged.
   - Else they read the CALLER's own `sys_user` row: `where.id` is the settings context's `userId`, never a body value, and the read projects one column (`email` or `phone_number`) under the system context. The disclosure is the caller's own address, to the caller, on a namespace-write-gated action whose holder can already name any `to`.
   - `sys_user.phone_number` is a declared field (`sys-user.object.ts:861`).
   - Every remaining refusal says nothing was sent and what to supply. A failed read is reported as a failed read.
   - The `from_email` fallback is retired. It sent the test to the sender's own, often unread, mailbox. The changeset states this.
   - The phantom `ctx.body.to` read is removed. `SettingsContext` has no `body`, and the handler context is typed `{ userId?: string }`.
3. **Two `sms/test` riders**, each a published defect the default recipient makes reachable from the served form:
   - a send through the log-only transport now answers `ok: false`, severity `warning`, which is `mail/test`'s rule;
   - the success message names the transport that carried it, not "via log".
4. **Pins and ablations.**
   - `mail-test-recipient.pin.test.ts` and `sms-test-recipient.pin.test.ts` boot a real `SettingsService` with the real manifests and `registerSettingsRoutes`, plus the plugin's real action registered at `kernel:ready`. They press `POST /api/settings/NS/test` with the console's body and assert:
     - the default-to-self recipient, with the read pinned to the caller id and one column;
     - the explicit-`to` control, which reads no account;
     - each refusal's ADR-0112 envelope with nothing sent.
   - Four ablation legs each turn red as predicted, with their controls green:
     - the `from_email` fallback put back;
     - the caller id withheld;
     - the log-transport check off;
     - `via` restored.
   - Every restore was proven by blob equality.
5. **Changeset**, `@objectstack/plugin-email` and `@objectstack/service-sms` `patch`, read sentence by sentence:
   - what was wrong;
   - the new recipient rule and its refusals;
   - the phone-sign-in caveat;
   - the log-only answer and the transport name;
   - "Unchanged": no key, route or setting is added, the provider choice is unchanged, and the save rule is unchanged.

   Each matches 2 and 3.
6. **Gates.** At ACCEPT, every check-run on this head is `success` or an expected skip, among them TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1–6/6, Build Core and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Locally, 76 of 76 derived families exited 0, including `check:engine-double-contract` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`. plugin-email 577 of 577, service-sms 103 of 103.
7. **The dev's open questions.**
   - **Half B (a Mail save with untouched, empty required fields answers 200):** measured as `validatePatch`'s documented TOUCH gate, not a defect. The dev recommends A (keep the gate), with C (console-side) as objectui's call, and says the axes conflict on making AI mistakes harder, where B (judge an untouched UNSET required field) is strongest. Under the decision frame, a conflict between the axes goes to the maintainer. This PR leaves half B unchanged. The card stays open, and the seat puts half B to the maintainer on #24767 when this lands.
   - **A recipient input on the page:** A, no new surface. API callers pass `to`, and default-to-self serves every mail admin and every SMS deployment with phone sign-in. Reopen as B (a declared transient action input) only on a named consumer: an SMS deployment without phone sign-in.
8. **Accepted deviations.**
   - `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains 2 rows through the gate's own prescribed `--write`. That is outside the named surface, and the new real-path pin needs it.
   - The two `sms/test` riders (3).
   - The gates were run under the verify lock, which is the conservative reading.
   - One merge of `main`.
   - The HotCRM evidence directory was not read (the classifier refused it). Half B was measured independently on a real `SettingsService`.
   - Commit trailers are model-free, per AGENTS.md.
9. **Out-of-scope dispositions.**
   - The console ignores an `action_button` handler's declared `body`, `url`, `method` and `confirmText`. Zero pull today: `Acceptance notes`.
   - The service-settings fallback `smsTestActionHandler` still answers `ok: true`, reachable only in a host-injected-transport composition. That is an inference, not a measurement: `Acceptance notes`.
10. **Landing clause.** Tier S: not governed, under the human-merge threshold. Next step: ready + auto-merge through the relay once every check on the current head is green or an expected skip. A push resets this reading.
